provenance.instrument: West Lampeter Township Code Chapter 285 Zoning (Ord. No. 270, adopted 6-5-2024), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 code date 2025-11-10 (breadcrumb). Chapter 285 adopted 6-5-2024 by Ord. No. 270, which repealed the 2006 zoning chapter. New Laws on 2026-11-14: none.
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 breadcrumb 'Code 2025-11-10'. Chapter 285 history: adopted 6-5-2024 by Ord. No. 270.
checks: 'Accessory dwelling unit' is a special exception (Zoning Hearing Board) in the A, C, RR, R-1, R-2 and R-3 districts (285-35C to 285-39C, 285-41C)

One ADU per single-family detached dwelling, for use by a relative (spouse, sibling, parent, child, grandparent, great-grandparent, grandchild, great-grandchild, uncle, aunt, niece, nephew, sibling-in-law, parent-in-law or first cousin) (285-49D(1)(a), 285-33)

The owner lives in the house or the ADU. Annual written certification with a fee, a recorded agreement limiting occupancy, and the permit ends when the owner or relatives leave or the property is sold. Then the ADU is reconverted into the house or removed (285-49D(1)(b), (c), (i), (j), (l))
Contained in or attached to the house, which keeps the look of a single-family detached dwelling. Added entrances on the side or rear (285-49D(1)(e), (f))

At most 40% of the house's total floor area or 800 sq ft, whichever is less, and two bedrooms (285-49D(1)(g)). In the A district a larger ADU, up to 60% or 1,200 sq ft, whichever is less, may be approved as a conditional use by the Board of Supervisors (285-49D(1)(m))

The definition of dwelling unit asks for at least 800 sq ft of habitable floor area, primarily above the ground level, and says a dwelling unit may not include two separate sets of kitchen facilities or living areas closed off from each other by interior walls (285-33). Read with the 40% or 800 sq ft cap, an ADU that counts as its own dwelling unit would need exactly 800 sq ft and a house of at least 2,000 sq ft. Where provisions differ, the more restrictive applies (285-64). Ask the zoning officer
One more off-street parking space for the ADU, beside the house's two (285-49D(1)(d), 285-27)
Any on-lot sewage system is certified by the Sewage Enforcement Officer with the ADU added (285-49D(1)(h))
R-1, R-2 and R-3 lot sizes and side yards depend on public water and sewer (285-37E to 285-39E)

Conversion of a building into dwellings: by right in MS ('Conversion of existing building into dwellings', 285-43B(1)(e)), while 285-48A(16)(a) makes converting a house that existed on March 14, 1978 into a two-family dwelling a special exception in the RR, TV and MS Districts. The R-3 use list names the conversion apartment as a special exception (285-39C(1)(c)). The RR and TV use lists do not. Lot area doubles, 800 sq ft per unit, three parking spaces per unit (285-48A(16))
Duplex dwellings are permitted in R-2 and R-3. In the A district a lot may hold two single-family detached dwellings if each could be subdivided onto its own conforming lot (285-19B(2)(b))
Elsewhere relief is a Zoning Hearing Board variance (285-60.1D(3)). The unlisted-use special exception (285-64B) reaches only uses listed in no district, so not an ADU
provenance.notes: Zoning office: West Lampeter Township Zoning Officer. eCode360 code WE2002 is West Lampeter Township (the only West Lampeter in Pennsylvania, in Lancaster County). Read on eCode360 in a browser, one page at a time, on 2026-11-14. Code search (all content) for 'accessory apartment', 'accessory dwelling', 'in-law', ECHO, 'elder cottage', granny, 'sleeping quarters', 'immediate family', 'accessory living', 'guest house', 'tenant house', caretaker, relative, relatives, 'family member', 'living quarters', 'housekeeping unit' and 'family dwelling' found the ADU listings and definitions. A search for 'accessory dwelling unit' found the six district sections and 285-49. A search for 'conversion apartment', 'duplex dwelling', 'two-family', 'not specifically', 'unnecessary hardship', 'two single-family' and 'immediate family' found 285-48A(16), 285-19, 285-64 and 285-60.1. A search for 'accessory apartment', 'neighborhood development', 'carriage house' and 'granny flat' found 'accessory apartment' only in the parking table (285-27: 'Single-family detached dwelling with an accessory apartment within a neighborhood development', 3 spaces for the two units), with no section that permits such an apartment. Read in full: 285-19, 285-35 to 285-39, 285-41, 285-48A(16), 285-49, 285-64, definitions of dwelling types, dwelling unit, related or relative, lot coverage. Read in part: 285-27, 285-60.1. Fix round on 2026-11-14 after an independent review: read 285-43 (MS) in full, 285-48A(16) and 285-49 again, the 285-33 dwelling unit definition, and searches for 'conversion apartment' OR 'conversion of existing' (only R-3 and MS list it) and 'more restrictive' (285-64). Not read: TV (285-40) in full and the commercial and industrial districts (search excerpts only: TV and I/M list single-family dwellings, no ADU. The independent review read TV and MS and found no ADU), the special exception criteria in 285-6 and Article VIII, the district summary attachments and the zoning map (PDF). Second review, 2026-11-26: legislation through 11-10-2025; New Laws lists Ord. No. 274 (intermunicipal agreement) and 275 (Chapter 34), no zoning change. The whole chapter was read in one print view and searched by section for accessory dwelling, accessory apartment, apartment, in-law, ECHO, elder, conversion, two-family, duplex, caretaker, tenant and farm employee: ADUs are listed in A, RR, R-1, R-2, R-3 and C (285-35 to 285-39, 285-41, 285-49), duplexes in R-2, R-3 and I/M, conversion of existing buildings in MS (285-43), conversion apartments in 285-48A(16); TV (285-40) and the commercial districts list no ADU. Left for a later check, each shown as a condition or a disputed reading: the 800 sq ft dwelling unit minimum (285-33) against the 40% or 800 sq ft cap, the districts the conversion apartment reaches, and the parking row for an accessory apartment 'within a neighborhood development' (285-27).

value.name: Conversion apartment: a house that existed on March 14, 1978, converted into a two-family dwelling
value.conditions: Zoning Hearing Board special exception. The single-family detached dwelling existed on March 14, 1978. Lot area at least the district minimum times the number of families. Each unit at least 800 sq ft of habitable floor area. No external alteration except for safety. At least three parking spaces per dwelling unit. Drawings and agency certificates where a family lives above the ground floor. On-lot sewage capacity shown and reviewed by the Sewage Enforcement Officer. No family or owner rule.

value.name: Conversion of an existing building into dwellings (MS)
value.conditions: 'Conversion of existing building into dwellings' is a permitted primary use in the MS Main Street District. A conversion apartment is a new dwelling unit created within an existing building within the standards of Article V, with the floor area of 285-19 (285-33). Each dwelling unit needs at least 800 sq ft of habitable floor area (285-33, 285-48A(16)(a)[5]). MS residential lot: 7,000 sq ft with sewer and water, 55 ft wide, yards 25, 15 (30 both sides) and 25 ft. If 285-48A(16) applies, the lot needs 7,000 sq ft per family (14,000 sq ft for two units), the house must have existed on March 14, 1978, no external alteration except for safety, and three parking spaces per unit

value.name: Duplex dwelling in R-2 or R-3
value.conditions: A duplex is 'A building that includes two dwelling units and which is not a twin dwelling', typically one unit above the other. Permitted in R-2 and R-3 (in R-3 fewer than 10 units). Ten or more new dwellings need a conditional use. Each dwelling unit needs 800 sq ft of habitable floor area and two parking spaces.

value.name: Second single-family detached dwelling on an A district lot
value.conditions: A lot in the A District may include two single-family detached dwellings if each could later be subdivided onto its own conforming lot (lot area, yards and width). Each dwelling lot needs 35,000 sq ft, 200 ft of width and yards of 50, 25 and 50 ft. The tract's quota of new principal uses (285-35L) also applies.
value.note: Not an ADU listing. A second house, not an accessory unit. The 70,000 sq ft figure is two 35,000 sq ft lots, a reading

value.name: Larger ADU in the A district by conditional use
value.conditions: In the A-Agricultural District an ADU of up to 60% of the principal dwelling's total floor area or 1,200 sq ft, whichever is less, may be approved as a conditional use by the Board of Supervisors. It keeps the architectural design, style, appearance and character of the house, and an addition beyond the current footprint or height matches the facade, roof pitch, siding and windows. All other ADU standards apply: a relative, owner-occupied, in or attached to the house, two bedrooms, one more parking space
value.note: The standard ADU (40% or 800 sq ft) is a special exception from the Zoning Hearing Board. This larger one is a hearing before the Board of Supervisors

value.condition: For use by a relative: spouse, brother, sister, parent, child, grandparent, great-grandparent, grandchild, great-grandchild, uncle, aunt, niece, nephew, sister-in-law, brother-in-law, parent-in-law or first cousin (blood, marriage, adoption or formal foster relationship). Not second or more distant cousins.

The owner lives in the house or the ADU as the owner's primary residence. Each year the owner certifies compliance in writing with a fee. A recorded agreement with the Township limits occupancy. The permit is revoked automatically when the owner or the relatives move out or the property is sold, and a new owner must apply again. If the rules are not met the ADU is reconverted into the house or removed.

Contained in, or attached to, the principal dwelling. The building keeps the appearance of a single-family detached dwelling, and any added entrances or exits are on the side or rear. At most two bedrooms.
Any on-lot sewage system is certified by the Sewage Enforcement Officer to meet all requirements with the ADU added.

The definition of dwelling unit asks for at least 800 sq ft of habitable floor area, primarily above the ground level (285-33). The ADU cap is 40% of the house or 800 sq ft, whichever is less (285-49D(1)(g)). On a house under 2,000 sq ft the two cannot both be met, and the more restrictive provision applies (285-64). Ask the zoning officer whether the 800 sq ft minimum reaches an ADU

max_sqft.note: 'shall not exceed 40% of the principal dwelling total floor area or more than 800 square feet, whichever is less, nor have more than two bedrooms.' In A, up to 60% or 1,200 sq ft by conditional use (285-49D(1)(m)).

max_share_of_house.note: Whichever is less of 40% and 800 sq ft.

min_sqft.note: The definition of dwelling unit requires 'a minimum of 800 square feet of enclosed habitable, indoor, heated floor area, which shall be primarily above the ground level'. If the ADU counts as a dwelling unit, this conflicts with the cap of 40% of the house or 800 sq ft, whichever is less: only exactly 800 sq ft on a house of at least 2,000 sq ft would meet both. The same definition says a dwelling unit may not include two separate sets of kitchen facilities, or living areas completely separated by interior walls. Where provisions differ, the more restrictive applies (285-64). Ask the zoning officer
